text:
'Passive movements' are movements of a body part produced by an external force—such as a therapist, machine, or gravity—rather than by the person's own muscle contraction. They are used in physical therapy and clinical assessment to maintain range of motion, prevent stiffness, and evaluate joint mobility or tone. The team note is incorrect: passive movements are not defined as movements against resistance that stretch the joint at end range.
